mods.name: Audio Engine
mods.desc: Audio engine: scene music, sound effects and ambience on separate buses with their own volume, and a music player that follows the current scene.

mods.name: Avatar Engine
mods.desc: Reusable avatar definitions and independent preset state, with renderer-neutral composition for layered images and animated models.

mods.name: Layered Avatars
mods.desc: Layered PNG avatar renderer: preset-controlled images, ordering, placement, visibility and opacity.

mods.name: Battle Formulas
mods.desc: Battle skills written as data: damage and heal formulas over the participants' stats, resource costs, pierce and stun — no code, and the same skill works in every battle core.

mods.name: Card Battle
mods.desc: A battle system with cards: pick a character card and drag its action cards onto targets. Built on Turn Battle Base; the battle of Cthangover.

mods.name: Catalog Export
mods.desc: Export mod catalog metadata and installable archives.

mods.name: Characters Engine
mods.desc: Characters engine: heroes, companions and enemies with their battle attributes and action cards, the character actions panel and dialog portraits.

mods.name: Characters Editor
mods.desc: Edits a mod's characters while the game runs: names in every language, portrait, RPG walking sprite, battle numbers and actions. A save reaches the running game at once.

mods.name: Classic RPG Rules
mods.desc: A ready set of classic fantasy rules as data: six attributes, three classes, equipment slots, gear and four formula skills. RPG Plus is built on it.

mods.name: Cooking
mods.desc: The kitchen of Cthangover: learn recipes, cook at the home_kitchen workbench and keep an eye on the party's rations.

mods.name: Crafting
mods.desc: Workbench stations that turn materials into items: stations and recipes are plain data, and any scenario opens a station with one command.

mods.name: Cthangover: Story
mods.desc: The story content of Cthangover: scenes, scenarios, characters, items, quests and the world map of Marao's very bad night. The machinery lives in engine mods.

mods.name: Cthangover: Murakami
mods.desc: A Cthangover story line: follow the beast prowling the town to a meeting with Murakami — scenarios, her character and expressions, a journal quest and battles.

mods.name: Dialog Engine
mods.desc: Dialog engine: the dialog box with portraits and answers, and the .scenario language in which every game of the collection tells its story.

mods.name: Editor Tools
mods.desc: Compatibility toolset: installs the individual scene, scenario, map, interactive, light, Godot scene and catalog tools.

mods.name: Effects Engine
mods.desc: Scene effects and continuous atmosphere: editable particle profiles and extensible emitters for leaves, fireflies, snow, rain and dust.

mods.name: Effects Editor
mods.desc: Live atmosphere authoring: particle and ripple profiles, preview, map and cell placement.

mods.name: Equipment
mods.desc: Wearable gear for any game with stats: slots as data, items become equipment by their JSON keys, and worn bonuses flow into sheets, battles, checks and conditions at once.

mods.name: Expression Engine
mods.desc: Reusable numeric expressions with mod-defined function and operator strategies, strict runtime assignments and compatible game formulas.

mods.name: FF Battle
mods.desc: A battle system in the style of classic console RPGs: the party, the enemies and a command menu — Attack, Items, Defend, Escape. The battle of RPG Plus.

mods.name: Interactive Base
mods.desc: Clickable objects for picture scenes: a picture of its own over the background, a glow under the mouse, and a click that starts a scenario.

mods.name: Interactive Editor
mods.desc: Edit scene interactive objects and their placement on backgrounds.

mods.name: Items Base
mods.desc: Items and the inventory: what an item is, the bag panel, what is saved, and scenario commands to give, take and check items.

mods.name: Items Editor
mods.desc: Edits a mod's items while the game runs: names and descriptions in every language, price, picture, types and the use action. The game shows a save at once.

mods.name: Junior Reaper & Paper Grief
mods.desc: Расследование повторных смертей стражника: фэнтезийный RPG-мир, осмотр мельницы мышью, сброс, свидетели и решение семейной причины.

mods.name: Light Editor
mods.desc: Edit scene lights and their placement on backgrounds.

mods.name: Live2D Cubism
mods.desc: Live2D Cubism runtime for C#: drawn characters that breathe, blink and move with physics, playing the motions and expressions their artist made.

mods.name: Locale Atlas
mods.desc: Maps every translation key of every mod: what each language declares, where keys are used, and what is wrong — missing, empty, undeclared or duplicated keys and encoding problems.

mods.name: Locale Editor
mods.desc: A translations window: lists every text a language lacks (from the locale atlas), and writes the translation into the locale file of the mod that owns the key, so the game shows it at once.

mods.name: World Map Engine
mods.desc: World map engine: a full-screen picture of the world with places to travel between; scenarios open, close, hide and reveal them as the story goes.

mods.name: World Map Editor
mods.desc: Edit world map zones, polygons, labels and markers.

mods.name: Menu
mods.desc: The main menu: start or continue a game, pick one of the installed games, load a save and change the language, sound and display settings.

mods.name: Mod Manager
mods.desc: The Mods & Collections screen: what is installed, what each mod does, installing and updating from the online catalog, and which mods make up each ready-made game.

mods.name: Music Pack
mods.desc: Shared music for any game: 22 tracks with exploration, combat and main menu playlists; a game can override playlists while keeping the track names.

mods.name: My Novel
mods.desc: The novel template's content: an evening town, a bar and a home connected by choices. Copy it, rename it and grow your own story from these three places.

mods.name: NPC Ambient Scenarios
mods.desc: Concurrent ambient scenario hosts, speech cues and NPC attention. Prototype.

mods.name: Quests Engine
mods.desc: Quests engine: quests with numbered steps that scenarios start, advance and finish, and the journal panel that shows them.

mods.name: Recruiting
mods.desc: Defeated enemies can be captured after a victory and later fight on the player's side; while they wait in the recruits list, they live by rules of their own.

mods.name: Resource Atlas
mods.desc: Maps which mod uses whose resources and whether every link is backed by depends — catching undeclared dependencies and duplicate providers no depends order can settle.

mods.name: RPG World
mods.desc: A walkable tile world in the spirit of RPG Maker: grid movement with WASD, events on E/F, teleports; a map is an ordinary scene of the game. Battles and random encounters come with turn_battle_base through the battles integration, so the world runs without it.

mods.name: RPG Map Editor
mods.desc: RPG map editor for model v2 (plan 12.4): a palette by shape, the map in the game's own top-down and isometric projections, placements (own and foreign, as patches), strokes, collision, spawn, teleport links, undo and a byte-stable save; encounters when rpg__battles is mounted.

mods.name: RPG Object Editor
mods.desc: Edits RPG objects (model v2) while the game runs: surfaces, segments, sprites and actors in a form by shape, their pictures, footprint, anchor, interaction and extends, with a preview in the top-down and the isometric projection drawn by the game's own renderer. A foreign object is edited as a patch in the own mod; the source stays untouched.

mods.name: RPG Plus
mods.desc: A complete small RPG: a prologue that picks the class, a village and forest mystery, crafting, trade, a desert and turn-based battles — data and scenarios only.

mods.name: Scenario Editor
mods.desc: Edit scenario text and transition graphs, then play-test inside the current game.

mods.name: Scenario Studio
mods.desc: A dock beside the running game that pauses, steps and edits the playing scenario: breakpoints, restarts with state rollback, live edits into a mod or a per-game layer.

mods.name: Scenario Authoring Base
mods.desc: Shared scenario file access, syntax and graph models for authoring tools. No tool windows.

mods.name: Godot Scene Builder
mods.desc: Inspect and edit Godot scene nodes and their properties with a live preview.

mods.name: Scene Editor
mods.desc: Create and edit logical scenes, backgrounds, ambient sound and scenario bindings.

mods.name: Schemas
mods.desc: Lets every mod describe its scenario actions, DSL commands and data fields as data; the tools build forms, pickers and checks from these descriptions.

mods.name: Schema Tools
mods.desc: The Data Editor window and the command palette: edit any described entity in a form and assemble checked scenario lines from the mods' schemas.

mods.name: 2D Shell
mods.desc: The frame every 2D game is drawn in: the background view box, the toolbar, panel slots and notifications that content mods fill.

mods.name: Skills Engine
mods.desc: The player's collection of skill cards: skills that open possibilities in other mechanics, grant battle action cards and add up into the collection effect.

mods.name: Stat Checks
mods.desc: One scenario command, check: roll a character's stat plus dice against a difficulty and branch the story on success or failure.

mods.name: Stats Engine
mods.desc: A stats engine for any genre: stats, archetypes and traits as data, formulas for derived numbers, character sheets, levels and pools — handed to battles unchanged.

mods.name: Test Defaults and Patches
mods.desc: A test fixture, not content: property patches the property_patches test loads to check how patches of other mods' characters and items merge. Never part of a game.

mods.name: Test Integrations
mods.desc: A test fixture, not content: hosts the integration 'probe' that joins a mod set only together with quests_base, so the tests can check both the boot and the in-process mounting gate. Never part of a game.

mods.name: Isometric Tiles
mods.desc: Draws tile maps at an angle, a grid of 2:1 diamonds, so buildings and trees stand up out of the ground. One of the two views of Tile Rendering.

mods.name: Tile Rendering
mods.desc: The shared engine behind tile maps: turns a prepared map description into a picture; the viewing angle is a small renderer mod on top.

mods.name: Top-down Tiles
mods.desc: Draws tile maps straight from above, on a square grid, in the style of classic 2D RPGs. One of the two views of Tile Rendering; RPG Plus uses it.

mods.name: Time Engine
mods.desc: The in-game clock, day and night: scenes change their look with the time, lamps and windows light them, and a portable lamp helps after dark.

mods.name: Tool Authoring Base
mods.desc: Shared forms, file access, localization editing and UI components for authoring tools. No tool windows.

mods.name: Town Pack
mods.desc: Ready-made scenery for a small-town story: the town entrance, a home vestibule and an evening bar as backgrounds, with the bar's ambience. No story inside.

mods.name: Trading
mods.desc: Shops as data and a trade window of two inventories: the merchant's goods on one side, the player's bag on the other, and money as an ordinary item.

mods.name: Turn Battle Base
mods.desc: The platform under every turn-based battle: starting from a scenario, the battle scene, victory and defeat, experience and loot — how the player fights is a separate battle system.

mods.name: UI
mods.desc: The interface layer every game shares: the toolbar, the in-game menu, the save indicator, notifications and the common look of panels, buttons and lists.

mods.name: Validator
mods.desc: Checks every mod without running the game: broken references, unknown scenario commands, wrong parameters, missing dependencies — a report on every game start.

mods.name: Village Pack
mods.desc: Reusable RPG objects and individual images: surfaces, vegetation, buildings, shared interiors, containers, walking sprites, battle artwork, snow enemies and editable atmosphere profiles.
